claim: The Visitor's first-day tour, unnamed trainee and imagined reactions are original illustrative framing at Carnuntum c.AD200, not a recovered individual's schedule.
limit: No invented dialogue presented as a quotation; no exact local daily timetable.

claim: Surveyed remains west of Carnuntum's civilian amphitheatre are interpreted as a gladiator school; its plan includes a controlled entrance and circular training structure.
locator: Antiquity pp181–185; official Gladiatur school paragraph.
limit: Retain interpreted/reconstructed framing. School identification is strong interpretation rather than every room's function proven.

claim: The circular structure is about19m across; a central feature may represent a training-post foundation.
locator: Antiquity p184 and VIAS opening paragraph.
limit: Post-hole interpretation is possible, not surviving wooden post. Do not exact-reconstruct tiers or post carving.

claim: Gladiators included enslaved people, war prisoners and voluntary recruits; joining voluntarily did not preserve ordinary freedom of action.
locator: Met Training; Seneca37.1–2; BM Valentinus discussion.
limit: Different legal situations; do not call all enslaved or all willing. No universal contractual rights claim.

claim: Seneca evokes arena recruits agreeing to endure burning, restraint and death by the sword, and mentions a defeated fighter appealing for mercy.
limit: Paraphrase attributed; moral rhetoric is not a Carnuntum admission checklist.

claim: Schools were managed by a lanista with support staff; instructors specialized in gladiator equipment types.
limit: No named local manager or recorded speech. Instructor's exact biography unknown.

claim: Gladiatorial training could use wooden weapons and a standing post before paired practice; a Cypriot lamp depicts post training.
limit: No exact weights, repetition counts or first-day training prescription. Lamp predates scenario and is from elsewhere.

claim: Secutor and retiarius equipment differs: enclosed plain helmet/large shield/short sword versus no helmet/net/trident/dagger and left-arm/shoulder protection.
limit: Comparative kit, not exact school inventory. Secutor is not a legionary; don't mix kits.

claim: Small rooms in the southern and western wings are interpreted as residential cells; exact occupancy is estimated.
limit: Single bed and blanket are illustrative; no exact number of residents or definite private room allocation.

claim: Northern facilities are interpreted as a heated training or assembly hall and a bath complex, supported by floor, furnace and drainage evidence.
limit: Not a confirmed gym with a documented bathing timetable; no health outcome inferred.

claim: Investment in training and facilities could coexist with severe control; a useful body was not necessarily a free person.
locator: Synthesis of compound plan, training and status evidence.
limit: Editorial interpretation, not claim every owner was benevolent or every fighter enslaved.

claim: Trained gladiators could be hired for shows; defeat did not invariably mean death and mercy was possible.
limit: No survival probability or promise; no assurance a first-day recruit fought immediately.

claim: Fame and fan recognition could coexist with low status, illustrated by named fighters on the Colchester Vase and Roman gladiator imagery.
locator: Met Arena; BM Valentinus fame discussion.
limit: No named Colchester fighter moved to Carnuntum; no claim a celebrity could simply leave.
